RagShortTexts: Genoese crossbowmen paired heavy steel arbalests with pavises, dominating European.

Variants.Content: Genoese crossbowmen were Europe's premier ranged professionals, hired by French, Sicilian, and Byzantine monarchs. Operating in pairs, one soldier deployed a towering painted pavise shield into the ground while the crossbowman wound a heavy horn-and-wood composite arbalest, capable of piercing knightly mail at point-blank range.

Organized into disciplined companies under civic podestàs, Genoese mercenaries demanded gold coin upfront. On naval decks or siege works, their suppressive volleys decided naval engagements across the Mediterranean.
Winding the cranequin ratchets draws the bowstring under immense tension. When a square-headed steel quarrel snaps loose, it smashes through padded gambesons like dry firewood.
